intro: You're a contractor running your own limited company and you need a bookkeeper who understands the paperwork that comes with it. You want someone local who can keep your invoices, expenses and VAT in order, and who knows how IR35 records should look. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK bookkeeper who will quote you directly, with the price on application.
need_heading: What contractors searching for a bookkeeper usually need
need_lead: A contractor's bookkeeping has to stand up to scrutiny from HMRC and from clients, so the day-to-day records matter.
needs: You need your sales invoices and expense receipts kept tidily so that your limited company accounts are straightforward at year end.
You want someone who understands VAT, including whether the flat rate scheme might suit you and how to handle it if it does.
You need your contracts and timesheets filed alongside your bookkeeping records to support your IR35 position.
You want a bookkeeper who is clear about where their work stops and your accountant's begins, especially on year-end accounts and tax advice.
You would prefer to deal with someone local or easy to reach, which is why you searched for a contractor bookkeeper near me.
context_heading: What to understand about bookkeeping for contractors
context: Bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.

Ask whether a bookkeeper holds professional indemnity insurance and which body supervises them. Good bookkeepers are also clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say that you are a contractor operating through a limited company and that you need bookkeeping support.
Mention whether you are VAT registered and whether you use the flat rate scheme.
Explain how you currently keep your invoices, expenses and timesheets, and whether you want to move to a different system.
Describe any IR35 arrangements you have, such as contracts with clients and how you record your working days.
Say whether you want someone local to you and how far you are willing to travel or work remotely.
Mention that you would like a quote, and that you understand the price will be on application.
questions: Which body supervises you for anti-money-laundering purposes, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
Are you a member of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers or the Association of Accounting Technicians?
How do you handle VAT for contractors, and would you advise me on whether the flat rate scheme suits me?
What records should I keep to support my IR35 position, and how do you like contracts and timesheets to be stored?
Where does your work stop and an accountant's begin on year-end accounts and tax advice?
How do you prefer to receive invoices and expenses, and how often would we review the books?

faqs.q: Do I need a bookkeeper who specialises in contractors?
faqs.a: A bookkeeper who regularly works with contractors will understand limited company records, VAT and the paperwork that supports an IR35 position. That said, bookkeeping is not a regulated title, so check their supervision and training rather than relying on a specialism alone.

faqs.q: Can a bookkeeper advise me on IR35?
faqs.a: A bookkeeper can keep your contracts and timesheets with your records and help you stay organised, but IR35 status is a matter of tax law and often needs an accountant's or specialist's advice. Be clear about where their work stops and an accountant's begins.

faqs.q: What is the flat rate scheme, and should I use it?
faqs.a: The flat rate scheme is a way of calculating VAT for some small businesses, but it does not suit everyone. A bookkeeper can help you keep records either way, but you should take advice on whether it is right for your circumstances.
